div.p: 1. To consider what course of action the U.S. should adopt in the event of full scale invasion from North Korea subsequent to the withdrawal of U.S. troops from Korea.

list.label: 4. a.
list.item: To encourage the Rhee Government to attempt the peaceful unification of Korea by direct negotiations with the North Korean regime.
list.label: b.
list.item: To begin planning and organizing now in order to bring into being at a later date a Korean underground task force in North Korea.
list.label: c.
list.item: To have U.S. naval forces visit Korean ports from time to time.

list.label: 5. a.
list.item: To implement current emergency evacuation plans to extricate U.S. nationals and military advisory personnel now accredited to the Government of the Republic of Korea.
list.label: b.
list.item: To present the problem to the U.N. Security Council for emergency consideration as a threat to the general peace.
list.label: c.
list.item: To initiate police action with U.N. sanction by the introduction of a military task force into Korea composed of U.S. units and units of other member nations of the United Nations with the objective of restoring law and order and restoration of the 38th parallel boundary inviolability.
list.label: d.
list.item: To reconstitute a U.S. joint task force in South Korea at the special request of the National Assembly of the Government of the Republic of Korea in view of the emergency situation.
list.label: e.
list.item: To extend and apply the Truman Doctrine to Korea.

list.label: 6. a.
list.item: That prior to military aggression, the U.S. Government should adopt the possible intermediate courses of action listed in 4a and c, above.
list.label: b.
list.item: That the U.S. should adopt the intermediate course of action 4b only if there is a sincere and responsive effort on the part of the Rhee Government to unify Korea without resort to force and such course of action (4a) is unsuccessful.
list.label: c.
list.item: That if a full-scale military invasion from North Korea becomes a reality, and the Korean Government is unable to successfully counter such move, the U.S. Government should adopt and implement the possible courses of action listed as 5a and b, above.

list.label: a.
list.item: This study be considered by the Joint Chiefs of Staff in assessing the military implications of the problem.
list.label: b.
list.item: The views of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and a copy of this study be forwarded to the Secretary of Defense for transmittal to the National Security Council for its consideration.
